newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel says deficit threatens forex regime.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel says deficit threatens forex regime.

text.p: A top Bank of Israel official said in a paper released on Monday that the government would have to abandon either its inflationary target or the exchange rate regime if it did not rein in the budget deficit.

"Failure to fulfil its decision on the budget deficit targets for a third year running means the collapse of the whole macro-economic strategy that the government decided on," said David Klein, director of the central bank's monetary division and widely regarded as the number two official in the bank.
Klein said it is already clear that another budget cut would be required in order to meet the deficit target for 1997.

The Israeli government is targeting a budget deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, or 9.74 billion shekels. But in January, one month into the fiscal year, the deficit was 1.28 billion shekels.

"According to the opening figures for Janury 1997 and the early figures for February 1997 there is great doubt whether it will be possible to meet the deficit target... without a cut in spending in the literal meaning of the word," said Klein.
"The government has not yet done this and its current actions indicate it does not seem to have any practical intentions of doing so," he said.

As a result, Klein said, the Treasury would have to choose whether it would now defend its inflation target, which calls for a rise of seven to 10 percent in consumer prices this week, or the exchange rate regime.

Current exchange rate policy allows the Israeli shekel to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Since mid-January, the shekel has been trading at the bottom end of the band. This has forced the central bank to intervene in the local forex market, injecting liquidity into the economy.
"If it is impossible to fulfil the decision about the deficit target -- and that appears to be the case right now -- one of the other decisions has to be given up," Klein said.
Klein reiterated earlier calls from Bank of Israel governor Jacob Frenkel to institute monthly budget reviews followed by immediate spending cuts apportioned equally among all the ministries.
